results.title: Cockroaches as Civil Sphere?
results.description: For past few decades, India has witnessed a dialectical struggle between two competing visions of national solidarity. On one side stands Hindutva, which seeks to construct Hinduism as a civil religion—a public, political faith that unites Hindus across caste lines while creating discursive Others: Muslims, Christians, and secularists. On the other side stands the civil sphere itself—the realm of universal solidarities, individual rights, and constitutional morality that emerged from India’s anti-colonial struggle and has been nourished by diverse progressive movements ever since.
